### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e8aa17382ed7c126a36aef8ab16e59e940f6aa3b` — the merge of head `30c29d52018f761cec96849d23057f7826cd626f` into base `3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e8aa17382ed7c126a36aef8ab16e59e940f6aa3b && git checkout e8aa17382ed7c126a36aef8ab16e59e940f6aa3b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda 30c29d52018f761cec96849d23057f7826cd626f && git checkout -B drift-repro 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda && git merge --no-ff 30c29d52018f761cec96849d23057f7826cd626f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3452dec2193920e6bf0b2a059f1feaf0d08befda
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `431705c8847d1b7d41f06a4dfe23162aa9ddbe25`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.jobs.test.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-job/src/cron-job-adapter.ts, packages/services/service-job/src/interval-job-adapter.ts, packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/package-commit-revert-path-package.dogfood.test.ts

PR #32563 (card #32411, claim 6814199730, dev report 6815770223), narrowing face: PR body and changeset both open a line with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path in the five files. The prose faces (`.changeset/32411-same-name-jobs-refused-at-bind.md`, `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`) are the seat's sentence-by-sentence ACCEPT; they are read here only to judge FROM → TO against the code.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The narrowing is what the code does.** `jobNameCollisions` counts the jobs `collectBundleJobs` returns whose `enabled` is not `false` by name; a name two or more share is refused. In `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` the refusals are computed once, after the scheduled-work switch, the job-service probe and the posture read, each logged at `error` with a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409, both existing); in the loop the skip sits right after the `enabled: false` skip and before every other limb, pushing to `refused`. The enabled test in the counter and in the loop is the same expression, so a job is counted exactly when the loop would reach the skip.
- **Rows A to F of the PR's table hold against the code.** A/B: a `preserve` composition's top level holds the body's flattened copy and the residual's own job, two enabled of one name, refused. C: two bodies' jobs reach the bound list as two (flattened copies, or pushed from the bodies when the top level holds none: `mergeCollection` claims identities from the top level only). D: no `packages[]`, the app is the one holder. F (#32071 pin): two bodies' pull jobs, refused at bind. The adapters replace by name as the FROM column says (`CronJobAdapter.schedule` and `IntervalJobAdapter.store` cancel first; `DbJobAdapter.schedule` delegates to both).
- **The cancel (row E) cannot reach another artifact's job.** It is `retireAppJobs`' existing keep-set rule, unchanged: it walks this `appId`'s own record on this job service and cancels by the key that app scheduled under; `claimJobKey` keeps a key in one app's record. So a refused name cancels only a job of that name this app scheduled in an earlier call of this process. That job is by construction never a twin of the current call (twins are never scheduled): it is the earlier version's single job, which is row E, and it is the same answer the function already gives a name that lands in `notScheduled`, `missingOrganization` or `failed`. A re-bind of the same twin artifact finds nothing to cancel. Another artifact holding the name (bare key or its package-scoped key) is in another app's record and is not touched.
- **CONTROL: a one-job artifact's scheduling is unchanged; its answer is not byte-identical.** With no shared name `jobNameCollisions` returns an empty map before reading any body, nothing is logged, and no loop limb moves. Two additive differences remain on every call: the result carries `refused: []` (also on the three `withheld` returns, which spread `out`), and the closing info line carries `refused: 0`. The whole-result equality in `app-artifact-handlers.jobs.test.ts` had to gain the member, which is the proof. Declared in the changeset's last sentence.
- **`jobDeclaringPackages` answers as before.** The body walk moved to `bodyJobDeclarations` verbatim; the no-`packages[]` branch, the bound count filter (`byName.has`) and the returned closure are the same statements. Its #32071 and #32355 assertions are untouched in the diff.
- **The three moved pins moved the way the PR says.** #32071 "two bodies": FROM each run 409 TO `refused: ['sync','sync']`, no run, one coded refusal naming both. #32355 "JSON-loaded": FROM `out.pulls` two and a failed run TO `refused` and no answer. #32355 "control: owner IS the declaring body": FROM the body's copy running as alpha TO refused, the one-holder attribution still asserted. The "controls" pin drops the `sync` run row. The fail-closed disabled-twin pin is unchanged and still asserts the enabled twin scheduled and its run 409.
- **Refusal pins assert `code` and `status`** (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409) on every new refusal case and on the moved #32071 pin; candidates are asserted for the two-bodies and single-package cases.
- **Census 0 confirmed by read.** One first-party job, `showcase_health_sweep` (`examples/app-showcase/src/automation/jobs/index.ts`); `examples/app-multi-package` declares none.
- **Dogfood flake: does not plausibly touch this diff.** The failing case, `[#29414] control: a writable package's edit commit restores its own row in place`, publishes an object twice and reverts a package commit over HTTP; the file names no job and no schedule. The diff adds one in-memory pass at job bind, reached only with scheduled work on and a job service present, over the showcase's single job. A false refusal would be deterministic, not a 5000ms timeout that passes alone. NOT MEASURED here; the PR-side `Dogfood Regression Gate` concluded `success` with its shards skipped, so the battery's own CI reading is the merge queue's.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch`, and `patch` is the level AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives: `Metadata-protocol: none` (no key, accepted value, default or metadata type moves; `packages/spec` is untouched; the pending #32071 and #32355 entries of the same refusal family declare the same pair), and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. Present: the `!` title on PR and changeset, the `**BREAKING**` paragraph with the FROM → TO fix (give each job its own name), and exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which `check-adr-0087-registration` admitted on this head (`BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing`). No other released package moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on this head: 53 runs, 1 red.** `Check Changeset` concluded `failure` (2026-11-12T05:00Z): `check-changeset-no-major` could not read the PR BODY's `Clause-②:` line (near miss, reason `describing`: the line names the key a second time, in "The Claim's `Clause-②: no` is the same declaration"), so the level axis is NOT MEASURED and the step refuses. Not a diff defect and not a merge-base red: the remedy is a body edit, a bare `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line with the explanation moved to the next line (the `Metadata-protocol:` line was read); the gate re-reads on the `edited` event, no push. Everything else is `success` or `skipped` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` 8/8, `Build Core`, `Build Docs` green; UI jobs, Temporal Conformance, the dogfood shards and the queue verdicts skipped by path or event).
- **Exported interface gains a required member** (`AppArtifactJobScheduling.refused`). Additive for a reader, and both in-repo callers discard the result; declared `Clause-②: no`, as the pending entries that added `pulls` and `missingOrganization` were.
- **Serial dependency.** PR #32567 (card #32412) edits the same two runtime files and adds a residual holder kind to core's `PackageScopedHolder`; the seat has ordered it first. This head will move when it lands, and the new head owes its own review.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relayed for `os-bill`).
- Security: none found.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes a refusal real that nothing gave before: the artifact with a shared enabled job name lost one job silently, and refusing at the one binder both doors schedule through covers the JSON artifact no build judged. Counting enabled jobs by name, never by content, is the #32355 rule and is stable across deployments (it does not depend on which services are present). It takes one working answer away, below.

must-fix: none.

should-fix:

1. **One moved answer is undeclared and unpinned: a shared name whose other enabled twin would not have been scheduled anyway.** The collision skip runs before the `missingOrganization` limb, `judgeJobPull`, the handler lookup and the `schedule` call. On `main`, a pair where one enabled twin does not bind (a pull whose mapping is missing or sourceless, a handler the bundle does not carry, no `organization` under `isolated`, a schedule the adapter throws on) scheduled exactly ONE job, which ran, with the other said at `warn` or `error`: no shared key, no silent drop. On this head neither is scheduled. The rule is still the right one, but the FROM the PR body, the changeset and the BREAKING paragraph give ("both bound under one job-service key ... the other never ran, with no log line") is false for this population, and it is the one population that loses a correctly running job. Fix: one row in the FROM → TO and the changeset, and one pin (for example an enabled pull that binds beside an enabled twin whose mapping the artifact lacks: FROM the first runs, TO both in `refused`).
2. **The changeset does not say which pending, same-release sentences it supersedes.** `32071-pull-reads-mapping-by-job-package` item 4 ("each run is refused ... and records the failure") and `32355-residual-job-twin-refused` ("Each run of such a job ... is now refused ... and the job run records the failure") are unreleased and will publish beside this entry; with both jobs enabled no run happens any more. The entry's "a pull pair FROM both runs refused 409" describes an answer no release carried. Fix in this changeset, as `32071-pull-reads` did for its predecessor: a "Supersedes, in the same release" sentence naming the two entries and the both-enabled case (their sentences stay true with a twin disabled).
3. **The PR body's `Clause-②:` line is not readable as a declaration** (③, `Check Changeset` red). Body-only; it must be green before the PR is requested ready or queued.

nit:

- **Residual representation, known follow-on (after #32567 lands).** The refusal's `candidates` are `package` holders only: the residual is folded into its owner package when a body carries the artifact's id, and is absent otherwise, so the list can be one entry for a two-holder refusal (rows A with no owner, B) or empty (a `packages[]` artifact whose residual alone lists the name twice and names no package); the message alone names the top level. This is exactly how `jobNameRefusal` on `main` represents it ("which no holder kind spells"), so it is consistent, not independently wrong; adapt to the residual holder kind once core has it, and pin the candidates of rows A and B then (today only C and D assert them).
- **Reason spelling.** A single-package artifact listing a name twice is refused as `ambiguous-in-environment` with one candidate, the app itself. Nothing reads the reason off this log line; accepted.
- **Holder list in a three-way case.** With bodies alpha and beta declaring the name, beta's disabled, and an enabled residual job, the message reads "holds 2 enabled jobs ... declared by" and then names all three holders, beta included. Accepted; the count and the run forms are right.
- **Install-local answers success for such a package.** `collectJobsWithoutBody` does not judge a shared name, so the install returns 200, the bind refuses at `error`, and an earlier version's job of that name stops. The dev noted it and did not file it; it is a door disagreeing with the binder about what it can run, outside this PR's file surface. Follow-up card.
- **Catalogue across the upgrade restart (read, NOT MEASURED).** The cancel reads the in-process record only, so on a `DbJobAdapter` deployment that ran the surviving twin before upgrading, its `sys_job` row stays `active` after the restart while nothing runs. The same holds on `main` for any job a new version drops across a restart; not introduced here. Worth a line on the follow-up card.
- **No pin that another app's job of the same name survives a refused name's cancel.** It holds by construction (per-app record); optional.

Round: delta on record 6815889291 (PASS at `431705c8847d1b7d41f06a4dfe23162aa9ddbe25`, should-fix 1 to 3 and the residual-kind follow-on). The delta is `582fcbfac` (the should-fix commit) plus a merge of `origin/main` `3452dec21`, which carries #32567 (card #32412). The prose faces (`.changeset/32411-same-name-jobs-refused-at-bind.md`, `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`) stay the seat's sentence-by-sentence ACCEPT and are read here only against the code.

### ① Derived judgments

It is pinned: `a twin that would not have bound still refuses the name` schedules an enabled pull beside an enabled twin naming a mapping the artifact lacks, and asserts `refused` both, `pulls` and `notScheduled` empty, no answer, no pull, and one `{ code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', status: 409 }` refusal. The dev reports the ablation red for it; not re-run here.
- **Should-fix 2 is closed.** The changeset ends with a "Supersedes, in the same release" paragraph naming `32071-pull-reads-mapping-by-job-package` item 4 and `32355-residual-job-twin-refused`. Both quoted sentences are in those files at this head, and the paragraph's scope is right: superseded with both jobs enabled, still true with one disabled (the fail-closed pin, unchanged).

- **The additive members are declared.** `refused: []` on every result (the `withheld` returns too) and `refused: 0` on the summary line are now in the changeset and the PR body, which the first record's CONTROL bullet asked of the FROM → TO.
- **The residual candidates match the #32412 ruling and `jobNameRefusal` on `main`.** Ruling 6812605181 on #32412: the residual is `{ kind: 'residual', ownerId }`, the artifact's id, never a `package` holder. `jobNameRefusal` on `main` builds `[...declaring bodies, { kind: 'residual', ownerId }]` and is handed `ownerId: appId`; at this head it is byte-for-byte `main`'s. `jobNameCollisions` now builds the same list: every declaring body as a `package`, then, where the artifact holds more jobs of the name than its bodies declare, `{ kind: 'residual', ownerId: appId }`; the fold of the residual's owner into the `package` list is gone. Row A gives `[package alpha, residual(beta)]`, row B `[package alpha, residual(alpha)]`, both pinned on both adapters (`{ kind: 'residual', ownerId: appId }`, with the fixture's artifact id).
- **Row B is not a breach of the ruling's "one-holder case unchanged".** That condition is about attribution (`jobDeclaringPackages` answers the body when the residual's owner is the one declaring body), and it is still pinned unchanged in both describes. The bind refusal counts jobs, and there are two: the body's and the residual's. Naming the body and the residual beside it under one id is what #32567 itself does for "B carries the id and declares the job" (`[A, package B, residual(B)]`).

  - Four of the five `[#32412]` cases are identical to `main`'s: no body carries the id, a non-declaring body carries it, the owner among several declarers, the controls.

With both twins enabled that run no longer exists, which is this PR's declared narrowing. The pin keeps all three assertions verbatim with the body's twin disabled, so the job that runs is the residual's `host_map`, the same job that survived on `main`. `jobDeclaringPackages` counts a disabled job, so the refusal is the same one. It adds the both-enabled half: `refused` both, no answer, the bind refusal's candidates `[package alpha, residual(top)]`. Nothing is dropped; #32567's PR body named this move for whichever PR landed second.
  - `scheduleAndRun` at module scope is `main`'s nested function plus the adapter parameter (default `CronJobAdapter`) and the logger in its return.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on this head: 57 runs; every check's newest run is `success` or `skipped`.** `Check Changeset` has two runs on this head. The first (2026-11-12T06:48Z) is `failure`, the first record's signature: the body's `Clause-②:` line read as a near miss, reason `describing`, level axis NOT MEASURED. The second (2026-11-12T07:22Z), after the body edit, is `success`: one declared-breaking changeset with its disposition, and the level step passes. The red run is superseded on the same head, not outstanding. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` 8/8, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and both `PR-body guards` runs are green; UI jobs, Temporal Conformance, the dogfood shards and the queue verdicts are skipped by path or event.

The code that moved since is reached only when an artifact holds a shared enabled job name (census 0: `jobNameCollisions` returns before it for every first-party artifact), plus `main`'s own commits, which the queue ran when they landed. The checklist still reads the `(narrowing)` battery as pinned to the head; whether the queue's run stands in for it is the seat's call, to be written into the ACCEPT either way.
